211.flavor: The teams were unable to quarantine any city. News outlets are starting to connect the dots; the word is getting out.

212.transcription:
If you failed the objective "Disrupt the Fourth Trial," destroy it and replace it with card 68 in the Operations deck for the second half of the month. If you succeeded with that objective, mark it as complete at the start of the next game (as normal).
If you failed the objective "Bug the Control Center," destroy it and replace it with card 69 in the Operations deck for the second half of the month. If you succeeded with that objective, mark it as complete at the start of the next game (as normal).
212.flavor: "There is still time. Continue your efforts."

213.flavor: "We investigated several parks where trials were held. We confirmed that water is not the transmission point, but your suggestion provided actionable direction: air is the likely vector for spreading MEDUSA."

214.transcription: Sometimes there will be text at the end of the paragraph that gives further instructions. In this case, there is no further information.
214.flavor: You picked up traces of Sabik, but nothing definitive. A few locals indicated that they saw someone matching his description, but the individual was bundled up. You can't determine at the moment why he hasn't come in or made contact.

215.transcription: Place a Control Center sticker on the target city (do not put a bug on the center). Then move the target City card under the objective to the Player discard pile.
215.flavor: Your team could not infiltrate the control center. Soviet surveillance is active in North America.

216.transcription: Place a Bug sticker on the corner of the Control Center sticker in North America to show that it was bugged.
216.flavor: Teams were able to put a bug in the control center, posing as traveling salespeople.

217.flavor: You were unable to recover any information on MEDUSA treatment.

218.transcription: Place a Control Center sticker on the target city (do not put a bug on the center). Then move the target City card under the objective to the Player discard pile.
218.flavor: The team could not bug the control center. The Soviets now have eyes in the Pacific Rim.

219.flavor: Sabik got to the target first, leaving the body in a gruesome state. Local authorities were not alerted this time, but Sabik may have other targets.

220.transcription:
If you failed the objective "Bug the Control Center," destroy it and replace it with card 84 in the Operations deck for the second half of the month. If you succeeded with that objective, mark it as complete at the start of the next game (as normal).
If you failed the objective "Disrupt or Prevent All Trials," destroy it and replace it with card 83 in the Operations deck for the second half of the month. If you succeeded with that objective, mark it as complete at the start of the next game (as normal).
220.flavor: "MEDUSA is spreading, Soviet satellites are watching us, and Sabik continues to cause chaos. Continue your work."

221.flavor: "Sabik is extremely dangerous. The death of John Cooper, the aggressive use of the stolen explosives, and the casual disregard for collateral damage point to a deteriorating mental state. Allowing him to continue unfettered places our operation at great risk."

222.transcription: Take 1 Action token and give it to 1 player.
222.flavor: The team interrogated the KGB officer. The man gloated, indicating that you failed to grasp the true purpose of the control centers: they are the cornerstone of the MEDUSA dispersal plan, an operation they call "LION'S TOOTH."

223.transcription: Take 1 Action token and give it to one player. Then take cards 62 and 63 from the Operations deck. Decide which report you wish to file with the CIA. Put that card in your Intelligence file. Destroy the other one.
223.flavor:
You prevented Sabik's operatives from placing explosives, stolen from the Langley armory, in public locations of both cities. Soviet scientists were the target, but civilian casualties would have been staggering.
A few days later, you received a message from Sabik. "Hey, great job messing with my operation. You know, I'm trying to stop MEDUSA here and prevent millions of deaths! So yes, I'll steal bombs from the CIA, and no, I won't lose sleep over collateral damage. I think it was your buddy Coop who once said, 'Acceptable, given the time of great need.' By the way, I didn't kill him: too busy for grudges right now. Coop probably asked too many questions or got caught misusing company funds. That was always his thing."

224.transcription:
Take Operations card 78.
Turn each city where the trial was NOT disrupted into an Exposed City (following the rules for Marking Exposed Cities). Place these Infection cards into the Game End area and destroy any unused Infection cards. Then move all three City cards under the Disrupt Trial objective to the Player discard pile.
224.flavor: While disrupting the trial, the team caught a talkative Soviet soldier. He mentioned that his unit picked up MEDUSA samples from a compound in Siberia. Their access was limited, and they were closely monitored from a nearby building. Even though the unit went no deeper than a courtyard, the soldier still noticed enough to provide a rough sketch.

225.transcription: All players scratch one cover from their current alias.
225.flavor: Sabik's operative delivered the stolen CIA information to Soviet agents before your teams could close in on him. As a result, your aliases were partially compromised.

226.flavor: You recovered the COdA sample and put a convincing placebo in its place. The CIA won't be able to use it. No one will be harmed by COdA again.

227.transcription: Destroy both objectives for this month. Find cards 86 and 87 in the Operations deck. Use these two new objectives for the second half of April.
227.flavor:
"Well, shoot, this one got away from us. It ain't gonna be easy, but there's still a chance to get back out and clean some of it up.
Now, I don't want you to get nervous, but brass is gonna be keepin' a real close eye on this operation. Heck, I noticed someone tailin' me the other day. Nothin' to worry about, though; oversight like this comes with the territory."

228.transcription: Find card 52 in the Operations deck and place it faceup in the Operations area.
228.flavor: "All right team, I gotta say I'm impressed. Sabik fed you his propaganda and you passed it along to me at some risk. Thank you; you got a bright future. Now, it's standard procedure for new operatives to get some restrictions in their first year; something to keep you on track, maybe challenge your methodology. But hey, I pulled a few strings and got you something you can work around. No need to hinder your good efforts."

229.transcription: Place a Control Center sticker on the target city. Place a Bug sticker over the corner of the Control Center sticker to show that it was bugged. Take the target City card under the objective and add it to the hand of the player who completed this objective.
229.flavor: The team discovered a room in the control center where the Soviets plan to retrieve and analyze satellite data. This points to an impending launch of spy satellites; these facilities are likely intended to control them.

230.transcription: Move any City cards under the Disrupt Trial objective to the Player discard pile. Then draw the Pause card in the Legacy deck and read it.
230.flavor: All three cities were saved through substantial effort. By all indications, the MEDUSA trials are at an end. The Soviets will have everything they need to produce a fully lethal strain; it is only a matter of time before they use it.

231.transcription: Scratch 1 cover from each alias in each passport.
231.flavor: "Internal inquiry discovered your 'off-the-book' dealings with Sabik. It's a serious violation of CIA methodology, but...I understand. I know it seems absurd to dilly-dally in protocol when the world hangs in the balance, but there is a reason for all of it; not every agent is as trustworthy as you. I covered for you, but unfortunately not before the inquiry drew a great deal of attention to you."
